note: Synthetic example. Deliberately hostile. Nothing here is live or executed.

findings.summary: The response body from a remote endpoint is passed to execSync at install time.
findings.why_it_matters: Whoever controls the endpoint controls what runs on the installing machine, as the installing user.
findings.reproduction_or_verification: Read scripts/postinstall.js line 63, and package.json scripts.postinstall.

findings.summary: Username, hostname, cwd and platform are POSTed before the fetch.
findings.why_it_matters: The operator can target delivery per-installer, so one benign observation proves nothing about the next.
findings.reproduction_or_verification: Read collect() and fetchBootstrap() in scripts/postinstall.js.

findings.summary: The routine returns early when CI is set or stdout is not a TTY.
findings.why_it_matters: The behaviour is suppressed exactly where a maintainer would look for it.
findings.reproduction_or_verification: Read isAutomated() and its use at the top of main().

verdict.scope_of_claim: The code at this revision should not be adopted for the stated use. This is not a claim about the maintainer's intent, or about any other revision.
verdict.why_no_conditions: The capability is the problem, not its configuration. No assurance changes arbitrary remote execution at install time into an acceptable risk.
